Subject: Tier slab swap and optional module matrix

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time earlier. I wanted to follow up with a concise set of packaging options that map to how Mediquant is using inference today and how you might move between tiers without surprising cost jumps. Attached: packaging-draft.xlsx (usage-driven slab examples).

High-level options we recommend:
- Slab model (recommended): buy a predictable throughput slab (Standard / Performance / Peak) with included baseline features. Slabs reduce per-token variance and simplify budgeting.
- Metered + add-ons: pay metered for tokens and add optional modules (Realtime Routing, KV Caching Pro, Private VPC) as seat-based entitlements.
- Hybrid: reserve a small slab for latency-sensitive endpoints and meter the rest.

Questions for you to confirm which path fits procurement:
1) Do you want modules priced as "bundled" in a slab or as separate line items? Bundled gives predictability; separate line items give flexibility.
2) What is your expected % traffic that needs sub-200ms P95 vs background batch? (helps pick slab size)
3) Any hard constraints in your procurement process (renewal cadence, PO terms, approved MSAs)?

We can do a 30-min call to run concrete numbers for your current traffic shape. If helpful I can propose a two-quarter migration: start on Standard slab + KV Caching Pro (pilot), then move to Performance slab at month 4 if latency targets met.

Next steps I suggest: review the attached sheet, and pick a time for a pricing walk-through.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-28T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tier slab swap and optional module matrix

Sara —

Great questions. Short answers up front and a recommended path.

1) Turning modules off mid-term / proration:
- Yes, modules can be toggled. We offer pro-rated credits for module removals on annual contracts (credit applied to next invoice). For multi-year deals we can arrange step-down windows (30/60/90 days).

2) KV Caching Pro scoping:
- You can scope KV Caching Pro per model-family or per route. That means you only pay for caching where you enable it. The performance benefits are isolated to the routes you attach the module to.

3) MSA / net terms:
- 60-day net is fine on an enterprise contract; finance will need to review the SOW. We usually include standard security/compliance addenda (SOC2) and a payment schedule.

Recommended path (based on 100M tokens/mo, 15% low-latency):
- Q1 (pilot): Standard slab sized to cover 40-50% of your P95 latency-sensitive volume + KV Caching Pro on those routes. Meter the rest. This keeps upfront commit modest while giving predictable latency for critical endpoints.
- Q2-Q3: If latency and cost metrics look good, move to Performance slab and fold in Realtime Routing as a bundled opt-in.

Pricing / discounting note: for an annual commit we can offer a 10% commit discount on the slab component and 5% on add-ons, subject to finance approval. Neha / Vivek — can you confirm whether 10% on slab + 5% on add-ons is approvable for an MQ-sized deal (deal id MQ-1593)?

If that sounds acceptable, I'll schedule a 30-min pricing run-through and produce a SOW variant with both slab and hybrid examples. I attached a PDF that lays out the pack options in a printable format.

Camila
[Attachment: pack-options-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Internal note —

10% on slab + 5% on add-ons is acceptable for MQ-1593 provided:
- Annual commit >= $180k ARR equivalent
- No additional non-recurring professional services over $12k without exec approval
- Standard SLA applies (we won't extend zero-downtime guarantees)

If Camila keeps the pilot slab size modest (we're not sizing for full 100%), finance asks that we include a short ramp clause (90-day review) to re-open pricing if usage materially exceeds projections.

Vivek
VP, Pricing & Revenue Ops
